response: There is still no dedicated solar and stellar astrophysics cluster. Papers on stellar granulation, stellar rotation, solar active regions, solar wind, and stellar nucleosynthesis are scattered across "Exoplanets and Planetary Science," "Solar wind plasma physics," "Compact Object Astrophysics Simulations," and elsewhere — they should all be consolidated into a single solar/stellar cluster. The "Compact Object Astrophysics Simulations" cluster is a catch-all mixing neutron star vortex physics, AGB stellar evolution, cosmic ray feedback in galactic disks, and nucleosynthesis — these belong in high-energy astrophysics, solar/stellar, and galactic/extragalactic respectively. The "Diverse Astronomical Observations Survey" cluster still persists and should be dissolved, with AGN variability and CGM papers redistributed to high-energy or galactic/extragalactic. The goal remains six clean clusters aligned with the six subject areas.
